posts.author: Carolyn
posts.content_md: ok, I have to ask....what exactly is it? Is it a lighting stimulator?

posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md:
> **Carolyn:** ok, I have to ask....what exactly is it? Is it a lighting stimulator?

It's a general 3D rendering program, with the important distinction that you don't model the scene interactively using a mouse, but write the code in the povray language. 

Most people these days expect everything to be easy and interactive and intuitive, but the price they pay is the power that programming code has. 

You can have a look at 

[http://www.povray.org/](http://www.povray.org/)

for details. I think povray is one of those gems that has largely been ignored, but one day it will have its day. I plan to put together a video tutorial to show how easy and powerful it is. I happen to think that for non-programmers, it's the best way to start programming.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
This POV-Ray stuff is so cool. Last night I made a 3D-Crosseyed illustration as it is so easy to just change the camera angle after the objects are drawn. It would also be very easy to create mulitple camera views for stereograms. Anyway, I wanted to keep the resolution, so I kept the file as a BitMap. The link is below. 

It is a reflection image planed hologram of a fractal illuminated with a red laser.

Enjoy!

Don't forget to cross your eyes to get the two images to overlap so you can see it in 3D.

[http://www.sketchys.com/HoloPage/HoloFi ... al3dsm.bmp](http://www.sketchys.com/HoloPage/HoloFiles/POVDraw/Final3dsm.bmp)

posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md:
Cool...

Yes, getting the images for a stereogram is a piece of cake. You can just use the animation and it will give you all the frames.
